New place new foods and new experiences
Sep 2016 • Family
First off the bat; this is where the "Tao Hong Kong restaurant" used to be. 

Anyway, it has been opened for a many months already and I finally made it to the dinner table in a Friday evening. 

From the outside ones cannot missed the Singapore Sea Lion statue and the foods display case. The inside isn't bad either as it is very cozy with cubicle seatings and perfect ambient.

The staffs are young and eager which is nice, but the level of services and attention to customers does have some room to improve because the foods came way way before the utensils, and the later has be asked. Also the condiments such as salt and pepper shakers are emptied. We sat by the window btw.

The foods;
-Chicken Cream Sauce Spaghetti was nice and required a tad of salt.
-Chicken Chop Nam Yang Rice was perfect and the rice was nicely done.
-Frog Porridge was a bit salty but came with free tea and watermelon, but I didn't see the tea.
-Honey Chicken Wings were a bit bland and no hint of Honey, perhaps the honey was used to make it crunchy? But it was a good eat.
-Oyster Sauce Mushrooms and Kailan was great, saucy and nice.

The Drinks; 
-Bugis Singapore thyme juice was refreshing and sour.
- Ice Lychee tea was also refreshing.and sweet.

The bill; all of the above cost us about 780, 000 VND which is about $36.00 usd for two.

So overall it was a nice experience and we will definitely be back for the other dishes.

Well, y'all enjoy and happy traveling 😋

Better than what we have at home
Mar 2016 • Business
Was so surprised to find a Bugis Singapore here in the heart of District 1 HCMC. It's like I'm back in Singapore. The staff who greets you at the entrance is decked out in Singapore Girl outfit. You will hear the staff greeting "huan ying guang lin" and "xie xie guang lin". The menu selection is similar to what you can find in Kim Gary or Xin Wang Hong Kong Café in Singapore. A selection of cheese baked rice, pasta with chops, fried rice with chops, etc. I ordered the Chicken chope with Nanyang Rice (not sure what it means by Nanyang Rice, but it tastes a little like fried rice, with less egg). Tastes surprisingly nice, I liked the rice as well as the chicken chop. The iced lemon tea was a little too sour though but still nice. All in all, a good place for a quick lunch/ dinner if you crave for something from Singapore.
